Let \(x=2-1001d\). Then \(a_9=x\) and \(a_{2011}=4-x\).  
Since the sequence is positive and \(d\ge 0\), we have \(a_1=2-1009d>0\), so \(0\le d<\frac{2}{1009}\). Thus
\[
x=2-1001d \in \left(\frac{16}{1009},2\right].
\]
We need minimize
\[
f(x)=\frac1x+\frac{9}{4-x}.
\]
Set
\[
f'(x)=-\frac1{x^2}+\frac{9}{(4-x)^2}=0.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{3}{4-x}=\frac1x \implies 3x=4-x \implies x=1.
\]
This lies in the domain, so the minimum is
\[
f(1)=1+\frac{9}{3}=4.
\]

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
